text:
Aaron (Customer): hey team — running into repeated billing + duplicate completions with your SSE stream. stream disconnects mid-response, client reconnects and ends up getting the rest *and* a full second completion on retry. this is happening for a user batch, so costs are spiking. any ideas?

Maya (CS): thanks for the ping, Aaron. can you paste the reconnect sequence from the client (headers + curl or fetch) and a snippet of the server response you saw? also which model + endpoint?

Aaron (Customer): model: rwd-3-stream (hosted). endpoint: POST /v1/streams/generate?sse=true
here's stripped client log (sensitive tokens removed):

```
> CONNECT 2026-01-24T15:12:01Z id=cli-7b
> recv: data: {"event":"chunk","id":"evt-1","text":"...the quick brown fox ..."}
> recv: data: {"event":"chunk","id":"evt-2","text":"... jumped over the l"}
> connection closed by server (socket reset)
> retrying in 300ms
> CONNECT (reconnect) 2026-01-24T15:12:02Z id=cli-7b
> send headers: Authorization: Bearer ***; Idempotency-Key: none; Last-Event-ID: evt-2
> recv: data: {"event":"complete","id":"evt-999","text":"... lazy dog. Full response: <same as earlier>"}
> afterwards client receives separate ingestion webhook with full transcript from server showing entire completion again
```

Maya (CS): ugh. saw something like this once — likely at-least-once semantics w/o proper idempotency. @Oliver and @Kai fyi.

Oliver (Eng): thanks @Maya. quick notes: SSE reconnect is currently best-effort resume using Last-Event-ID for *delivery* not for deduplication. if client reconnects without an Idempotency-Key we treat it as a new generation. last-event-id only helps to resume event *delivery* stream, not to resume token-generation state in the model. so client can see duplicated tokens if the new request finishes a generation we already partially delivered.

Kai (SRE): reproducer idea: start a long streaming completion that we intentionally interrupt after ~30% tokens, then reconnect the client with/without Idempotency-Key and observe whether server re-executes. Aaron, can you confirm the client sends Last-Event-ID and whether it also sends any Idempotency header?

Aaron (Customer): we weren't setting Idempotency-Key — client only sets Last-Event-ID automatically from the SSE lib. so that matches. is there a recommended pattern? our users want resume capability so they don't ask user to re-run prompts.

Oliver (Eng): recommended short-term: 1) set an Idempotency-Key per logical generation request (same key for retries). server will dedupe completed responses within a short window (30s) so you won't be billed twice for a replay. 2) on reconnect, prefer sending the Idempotency-Key AND Last-Event-ID. 3) if you need true token-level resume (resume mid-generation), we currently have experimental resume-token support but it's not stable for hosted customers — it requires the model runtime to serialize KV-cache and resume point.

Maya (CS): sending this advice to the customer: the Idempotency-Key approach should stop the duplicate completed payloads. but it won't magically let the stream pick up mid-token; the experience will be either: resume event delivery if server still has session OR return a deduped complete (no billing double-charge) if request was recreated.

Aaron (Customer): ok we'll try Idempotency-Key. can you give the exact header name/value semantics? and a curl example?

Oliver (Eng): use header: `Idempotency-Key: <uuid4>` and keep it identical for original + retry attempts. example curl:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Idempotency-Key: 9f1b2e6a-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456" \
     -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?sse=true" \
     -d '{"model":"rwd-3-stream","input":"Tell a long story...","max_tokens":1200}'
```

Note: if you reconnect and the server still has the session live, Last-Event-ID will help avoid re-sending already-delivered events. If the server lost the session, the Idempotency-Key tells the backend to lookup prior generation result and return it (deduped) rather than create a fresh run.

Kai (SRE): small caveat — the dedupe window is currently 60s for hosted (we keep ephemeral generation results cached). after that we may spawn a new generation even with the same Idempotency-Key (we should improve this). if you need longer dedupe windows, please escalate to enterprise/dedicated where we can attach persistent storage and stronger idempotency guarantees.

Aaron (Customer): that explains the billing spike — our client retried after 90s. will try header now. thanks.

Maya (CS): I'll follow up after they test. @Oliver — should we open an internal follow-up to add clearer docs + client examples? also consider a server-side warning when Last-Event-ID is present but no Idempotency-Key, to avoid this pitfall.

Oliver (Eng): good idea. filing a ticket now.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3248 — "SSE reconnects causing duplicate completions when no idempotency-key" assigned to eng-runtime

Oliver (Eng): action items:
- eng-runtime: add server log message when Last-Event-ID received without Idempotency-Key (short term).
- eng-runtime: add doc + examples for Idempotency-Key + recommended client flow.
- eng-ml: evaluate feasibility of stable resume-token (KV-cache snapshot) for hosted in Q2.

Kai (SRE): temporary mitigation we can push: extend dedupe cache to 2m for high-error customers on hosted, but that is risky for memory use. I'll coordinate if Aaron's tenant needs it.

Aaron (Customer): would appreciate the extension for testing window — our SDK is flaky on mobile networks and timeout/retry happens often.

Maya (CS): I'll request the 2m extension for Aaron's account and come back with results.

Aaron (Customer): thanks all. one more question: if we do Idempotency-Key but reconnect with a different client instance (new socket, different Last-Event-ID), can we still get deduped result?

Oliver (Eng): yes — Idempotency-Key dedupe is independent of socket. as long as the header matches and the dedupe window hasn't expired, backend will return the prior completion rather than create a new run. that should avoid double billing.

Maya (CS): next: I'll confirm with Aaron after his test and then we can close the thread. :thumbsup:
